chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Friendship with Nat and Nadine, and the name 'Coles'
summary: Simmons kept Nat's wife Nadine company; Nat began singing, and they discuss the 'Coles' name and Maria.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: After that broke up, that's when I went to San Diego. But I didn't go directly to San Diego now. Nat got a job some-

where as a single. I can't think of where it was. And his wife -- he would leave money with me to take his wife, Nadine, Shorty Nadine, he called her Shorty, wherever she wanted to go, if she wanted to go to the movies or a dance, or wherever. You know, he'd leave money. And the three of us were almost inseparable, you know. We all liked the same things, the same -- you know. And when he'd come home, we wouldn't be anywhere, we'd be sitting there, you know. Getting loaded off grass.

And he smoked grass, too, God bless the dead, until he started singing. Then he stopped smoking completely. To protect his voice, you know. We all have our little idiosyncrasies and things, I mean, but this is the truth.
At that time he still used the name Coles, with an s on it? That was his original name.
Originally he was Coles. And when he began to get popular, he dropped the S.
Oh, oh, oh, when he got popular, then he dropped it. King Cole. But when he had the band, it was Nat Coles.
That's what I thought, 'cause I know that Nadine still uses Coles, right?
Up until the time she did, she still --
And he and Maria were Cole.
So were the members of the band at the Ubangi largely members of the band that he -- Shuffle Along --
That he brought out here, yes.
And then, he went to play a single, and
And I would keep his wife company while he was gone.
